name: 6N137-000E
title: 6N137, HCPL-26xx/06xx/4661, HCNW137/26x1: 10 MBd high-CMR logic-output optocouplers
summary: A family of fast digital optocouplers: a GaAsP LED drives an integrated high-gain photodetector whose Schottky-clamped open-collector transistor gives an LSTTL/TTL compatible logic output at 10 MBd typical. Single-channel parts (6N137, HCPL-2601/2611, HCPL-0600/0601/0611, HCNW137/2601/2611) have an enable input; dual-channel parts (HCPL-2630/2631/4661, HCPL-0630/0631/0661) do not. Grades differ in guaranteed common-mode transient immunity, from 1,000 V/µs (6N137) to 15,000 V/µs at 1 kV, thanks to an internal shield. Packages are the 300 mil DIP-8 (through-hole or gull-wing), SO-8 and the 400 mil widebody DIP; the outputs run from a 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply, with all figures guaranteed from -40 °C to +85 °C. 6N137-000E is the single-channel 300 mil through-hole DIP in tubes, RoHS compliant, UL rated 3750 Vrms for 1 minute.

circuits.title: TTL/LSTTL to TTL/LSTTL interface, single channel
circuits.description: A TTL gate on the isolated input side, powered from VCC1 = 5 V, sinks the LED current: with its output low, current flows from VCC1 through the 470 Ω resistor into the anode (pin 2) and out of the cathode (pin 3) to GND1, and D1 sits between the resistor node and the gate output with its cathode at the gate. On the output side the open-collector VO (pin 6) is pulled up to VCC2 = 5 V by 390 Ω and drives a TTL gate powered from VCC2. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor sits across VCC (pin 8) and GND (pin 5). The enable pin 7 is left open, so the output follows the LED.

operation.text: Each channel is a GaAsP LED facing a high-gain integrated photodetector. The detector drives an open-collector output transistor with a Schottky clamp, so the output sinks current to GND when the LED is lit. An internal shield between LED and detector gives the guaranteed common-mode transient immunity, up to 15,000 V/µs at VCM = 1000 V on the -11 and 4661/0661 grades. Data rate is 10 MBd typical, and the output is LSTTL/TTL compatible.

Single-channel parts have an enable input VE on pin 7 that gates the detector output (strobing). VE high or open: the output is low while the LED conducts and high while it is dark. VE low: the output stays high. VE needs no external pull-up; when it is not used, connecting it to VCC improves CMR. Dual-channel parts have no enable.

A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor between VCC (pin 8) and GND (pin 5) is required next to each optocoupler. Its two leads together, from capacitor to pins, stay within 20 mm. The recommended layout puts VCC on the front side and the GND bus on the back, with the capacitor within 10 mm of the package and a resistor from the VCC trace to the output trace.

The LED is on at 5 mA to 15 mA (IFH) and off at 0 to 250 µA (IFL), or with its voltage held at or below 0.8 V. A new part switches at 5 mA or less (ITH 2.0 mA typical single channel, 2.5 mA dual); driving 6.3 mA to 10 mA gives the best performance and leaves at least 20 % margin for LED output loss over life. Pulses up to 50 mA lasting at most 50 ns are allowed from peaking circuits while the average stays within the 20 mA (single) or 15 mA (dual) rating.
The output side runs from 4.5 V to 5.5 V. The pull-up resistor RL is 330 Ω to 4 kΩ; at RL = 1 kΩ one output drives up to 5 TTL loads.

operation.topic: Propagation delay, pulse-width distortion and skew
operation.text: tPLH is the delay from the input turning off to the output rising; tPHL is the delay from the input turning on to the output falling. Their difference is pulse-width distortion, which often sets the top data rate of a serial link. When several couplers carry parallel data with a clock, the spread of delays between units, tPSK, sets the rate: skew puts an uncertainty window on every data and clock edge, and a working link keeps the clock windows clear of the data windows. Clocking on both edges of the clock doubles the rate for the same clock frequency. These parts have tPLH, tPHL, PWD and tPSK guaranteed over the recommended temperature, input current and supply ranges.

CMR is measured with the circuit of Figure 15: a pulse generator drives the common-mode voltage between the input ground and the output ground while the LED is held off (IF = 0 mA, for CMH) or on (IF = 7.5 mA, for CML). CMH is the steepest common-mode edge for which the output stays above 2.0 V; CML is the steepest for which it stays below 0.8 V. Minimum CMR is 1,000 V/µs at 10 V for 6N137 and 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000 V/µs at 1 kV for the other grades.

The 6N137 is JEDEC registered, with the registration covering 0 °C to 70 °C. The guaranteed limits span -40 °C to +85 °C and are tighter than the registration for IOH (100 µA against 250 µA), ICCH (10 mA against 15 mA), ICCL (13 mA against 18 mA) and IEL (-1.6 mA against -2.0 mA).

UL 1577 recognition is 3750 Vrms for 1 minute for the HCPL parts and 6N137, and 5000 Vrms for 1 minute for HCNW parts and for option 020 (6N137, HCPL-2601/11/30/31, HCPL-4661). Each unit is proof tested for 1 second at ≥ 4500 Vrms (3750 Vrms rated parts) or ≥ 6000 Vrms (5000 Vrms rated parts). Option 060 adds IEC/EN/DIN EN 60747-5-5 approval with VIORM = 567 Vpeak for HCPL-06xx and 630 Vpeak for 6N137/HCPL-26xx; HCNW parts carry it as standard with VIORM = 1414 Vpeak. VISO is a one-minute withstand rating, not a continuous working voltage.

Surface-mount parts (SO-8 and option 300) are reflowed to JEDEC J-STD-020 with non-halide flux. Through-hole DIPs take 260 °C for 10 s at 1.6 mm below the seating plane; the widebody DIP takes 260 °C for 10 s up to the seating plane.

Typical uses are isolated line receivers, computer peripheral and microprocessor interfaces, isolation of A/D and D/A converters, switching power supplies, instrument I/O isolation, ground-loop elimination, pulse transformer replacement, isolation of power transistors in motor drives and isolation of fast logic systems, especially where ground noise or induced noise is high. A hermetic MIL-PRF-38534 version exists as HCPL-56xx/66xx.
The parts are ESD sensitive; handle and assemble them with normal static precautions.
